description: Explicit hypothetical financial and contract variants. These are proposed sources, not ten qualified tasks or ten demonstrated difficulty classes.

cases.name: Quarterly lock, cure and liquidity reserve
cases.mechanism: Baseline economics with quarter-nine entry, a two-quarter cure and higher reserve while locked. Require an economically binding first-pass lock and actual reserve funding, support and release.

cases.name: Short debt amortization and reserve release after payoff
cases.mechanism: Eighteen original amortizing payments and higher stated sales allow Loan A to clear. Require a subsequent actual zero-target reserve release rather than assuming that payoff or a cure occurred.

cases.name: Zero-interest Loan A with a still-active covenant
cases.mechanism: An explicit subsidized spread offsets Loan A interest. The reserve still uses the original zero-rate level payment, and the measured multi-facility covenant and cure govern distributions.

cases.name: Covenant starts after the commissioning quarter
cases.mechanism: The first contractual test is month twelve. Earlier quarter diagnostics cannot activate a lock or reserve. A later actual breach must still enter and cure under the unchanged two-successful-test rule.

cases.name: Higher coverage threshold prolongs the initial lock
cases.mechanism: A publicly specified 1.50 coverage threshold changes the test outcomes and reserve-holding period. No state flags are supplied as inputs, and financial feasibility is checked rather than repaired.

cases.name: Reserve only while locked
cases.mechanism: There is no normal reserve requirement and a five-payment reserve during a lock. Require an active unlocked zero target with positive Loan A and actual release of previously funded reserve.

cases.name: Cross-year commissioning interrupts the cure
cases.mechanism: Construction lasts twelve months, with service and amortization beginning in month thirteen and covenant tests from month fifteen. Require a failed test to reset a one-pass cure streak, followed by a real later cure.

cases.name: Startup losses and a binding annual NOL cap
cases.mechanism: Additional explicitly equity-funded startup expense changes tax and CFADS. Require the annual NOL cap to bind in the actual extended ledger together with a measured covenant entry and cure.

cases.name: Refresh funding precedes service across tax years
cases.mechanism: The refresh is paid in month fifteen but first depreciated in month twenty-five. The 1.60 threshold and two/four-payment normal/trapped reserve requirements are explicit contractual changes; their activation must be measured.

cases.name: Working-capital drag and interrupted higher-threshold cure
cases.mechanism: Longer receivable/inventory days and shorter supplier terms increase cash funding needs. A 2.20 coverage covenant requires an actual interrupted cure and a later observed two-pass release; reject the case if those paths do not occur.
